name: Drafting

tokens.name: vellum
tokens.usage: Page ground: cool drafting vellum by day, Prussian blueprint by night.

tokens.name: grid
tokens.usage: 24px drafting grid and hairline rules. Page grids use this at half strength; readable blocks have solid vellum backgrounds.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Line-work and primary text. 1px for construction, 2px for the object.

tokens.name: cobalt
tokens.usage: Hierarchy and annotation: headline emphasis, sheet numbers, dimensions, links and the primary action.

tokens.name: cobalt-soft
tokens.usage: Pale blue evidence panels, title blocks and selected regions of a drawing.

tokens.name: vermilion
tokens.usage: Fluorescent safety orange for revision fills, outlines and changed parts; use on-vermilion for text on the fill.

tokens.name: vermilion-ink
tokens.usage: Readable orange ink for revision text on vellum and pale orange.

tokens.name: vermilion-soft
tokens.usage: Warm orange ground for revision notes and changed regions.

tokens.name: positive
tokens.usage: Verified, passed, released. Always with a word.

tokens.name: caution-soft
tokens.usage: Warm fluorescent yellow for small assumption tags and short highlighted phrases; never a paragraph or full-width panel.

tokens.name: negative
tokens.usage: Failed or blocked. Always pair with a word.

principles: The object is drawn, not pictured.
Line-work in ink at 2px for the object and 1px for construction. Photographs are for marketing; a drawing is for understanding.
Figures attach to the thing they measure with a dimension line and arrowheads. A figure floating in a card is a rumour.
Cobalt leads; orange revises; yellow questions.
Use cobalt for headline emphasis, sheet labels and evidence. Orange marks a revision; small warm-yellow accents flag assumptions. Keep prose in ink on plain vellum.
The grid shows around the reading.
Keep the 24px page grid at half strength. Put readable blocks on solid vellum with generous inset padding; the grid remains visible in gutters and between sheets. Use d-reading for prose.
Each major part of the page is a sheet with its own title block: number, title, revision, scale. Reading the title blocks reads the plan.
